instantiated_cells.justification: The subchapter requires periodic expense statements to be filed by registered principals (not lobbyists), indicating there is no separate lobbyist periodic spending report requirement.
The only periodic filing specified is the principal’s semiannual expense statement; the statute does not require an annual lobbyist spending report.
No monthly lobbyist spending report is required; reporting is imposed on principals on Jan. 31 and July 31.
The statute specifies semiannual principal expense statements and contains no quarterly lobbyist spending report requirement.
Semiannual reporting is required of principals (expense statements each reporting period), not of lobbyists as a separate spending report.
No triannual lobbyist spending report cadence is provided; the only periodic report described is the principal’s semiannual expense statement.
The statute does not create any alternative ‘other’ lobbyist spending report cadence; it requires semiannual principal expense statements only.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in amounts the principal reports, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report reporting their total compensation.
The reporting statute breaks down expenditures by lobbyist within a principal’s filing, not by payer within a lobbyist’s own filing, and no lobbyist spending report is required.
The statute requires principals to file aggregate totals and certain listings, but does not require lobbyists to file an itemized periodic spending report.
Because no lobbyist spending report is required to be filed, the statute does not prescribe an itemized format for a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.
Any categorization/description of expenditures appears in the principal’s reporting requirements, not in a lobbyist periodic spending report (which the statute does not require).
The principal’s expense statement does not require lobbyists’ contact information as part of a lobbyist-filed report, and no lobbyist spending report is mandated.
The statute requires principals to file expense statements; it does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report listing principals represented.
Principal name and business address are part of principal registration, not a lobbyist periodic spending report, which is not required.
Descriptions of a principal’s business activity/nature are required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist spending report.
Reporting of legislative proposals/topics is imposed on the principal (reported to the commission), not as part of a lobbyist periodic spending report.
General topics/subjects of lobbying communications must be reported by the principal to the commission, not by lobbyists in a periodic spending report.

Identification of each legislative proposal/proposed administrative rule number is a principal reporting obligation, and the statute does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report including such identifiers.
While principals must report legislative proposals and proposed administrative rule numbers, no lobbyist periodic spending report is required to include bill numbers.
The statute requires principals to report proposals/topics but does not require disclosure of position taken, and there is no lobbyist spending report requirement.
The principal’s expense statement includes totals and time proportions by topic, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file spending reports allocating expenditures per issue.
The time record required in the principal’s expense statement covers meetings and activities but does not mandate a lobbyist-filed report of contacts made.
The statute largely prohibits furnishing such items and does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report disclosing gifts/entertainment/transport/lodging.
Indirect costs (e.g., overhead, travel/living) are components of the principal’s expense statement, but no lobbyist periodic spending report is required to include them.
The statute imposes filing of expense statements on principals and contains no requirement that lobbyists file a ‘no activity’ periodic spending report.
No lobbyist spending report is required, and the principal expense statement provisions do not specify reporting expenditures benefitting household members of officials.
